title: User cannot access shared drive after password reset
description: Employee reset their password via self-service portal and lost access to the department shared drive. VPN connects fine, other apps work.
root_cause: Password reset did not propagate to the file server's cached credential store.
resolution_steps: Ask user to fully log off and log back in (not just lock/unlock) to refresh cached credentials.
If unresolved, manually clear the user's cached credential entry on the file server via Server Manager.
Re-map the network drive from the user's machine and confirm access.

title: Application throws 500 error on login
description: Internal HR portal returns a 500 Internal Server Error when specific users attempt to log in. Other users unaffected.
root_cause: Corrupted session token for affected users after a recent SSO configuration change.
resolution_steps: Clear the affected user's session cache in the identity provider.
Force a re-authentication by revoking the user's active SSO session.
Confirm the SSO claim mapping still matches the portal's expected schema.

title: VPN disconnects every 10 minutes
description: Remote employee reports VPN client disconnects repeatedly, roughly every 10 minutes, since switching to new home router.
root_cause: Router's NAT keep-alive timeout shorter than VPN idle timeout, dropping the tunnel.
resolution_steps: Have user lower VPN client idle timeout below router NAT timeout, or enable keep-alive packets in VPN client settings.
Recommend user check router firmware for NAT session timeout setting and increase it if configurable.
If issue persists, escalate to network team to review firewall UDP timeout for VPN traffic.

title: Email attachments not sending
description: User unable to send emails with attachments over 10MB; smaller attachments work fine.
root_cause: Mail gateway attachment size limit set below the mail client's allowed limit, causing silent rejection.
resolution_steps: Check mail gateway's configured max attachment size against client-side limit.
Advise user to use the file-sharing link workflow for attachments over the gateway limit.
If business-justified, submit a change request to raise the gateway limit for the affected department.

title: Laptop running extremely slow after Windows update
description: Employee's laptop became very slow immediately after an overnight Windows update. High disk usage in Task Manager.
root_cause: Post-update Windows Search indexing service consuming disk I/O while re-indexing.
resolution_steps: Confirm high disk usage is from SearchIndexer.exe in Task Manager.
Let indexing complete overnight, or temporarily pause Windows Search indexing if urgent.
If disk usage doesn't subside after 24 hours, check for a stuck update or run disk cleanup.
